outcome: time of onset of adequate analgesia
complications (hypotension, pruritis, motor blockade, nausea, vomiting)
APGAR score at 1 min and 5 min
cohort: Pregnant women aged >18 years, ASA grade I and II, singleton pregnancy with vertex presentation with cervical dilatation of 3-5 cm and without any labor analgesia contraindication.
finding: Dural puncture epidural analgesia (DPEA) resulted in a significantly faster onset of adequate analgesia compared to standard epidural analgesia (EA), but there was no significant difference in the duration of labor, mode of delivery, or neonatal outcomes.
